subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call follow-up & sizing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Hi Olivia / team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — great discussion. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the dedicated-capacity performance validation we discussed.

Key SLOs you mentioned (confirm if anything needs to change):
- Streaming generation (server-side streaming to client) required
- Target p95 latency: <= 120–150 ms for single-stream responses (we'll validate p50/p95/p99)
- Sustained concurrency: 12–16 concurrent streams during peak (burst to 32 for short windows)
- Throughput sizing goal: baseline reserved throughput to support ~400–600 tokens/sec aggregated; autoscaling/burst policies for spikes
- Output quality: parity with your current endpoint (we’ll run side-by-side prompts)

Proposed validation plan (high level):
1) Redwood runs a 48-72 hour benchmark using your representative prompt corpus + live-ish traffic pattern (we'll need the test corpus and some sample traffic traces).
2) Compare two dedicated GPU configs: A100 80GB (current baseline) vs H100 80GB (preferred by your infra team) — we'll report latency percentiles, per-GPU tokens/sec, and memory/KV cache behavior.
3) Evaluate reserved throughput sizing to meet p95 latency target at your concurrency profile; include quantized model variants where applicable.
4) Provide a runbook + cost delta (reserved capacity pricing estimate) and recommended sizing for a first production commit.

Attachments: redwood_dedicated_sizing_v1.pdf (draft sizing + benchmark template), benchmark_template.csv (prompts + traffic mix template).

Next steps / asks:
- Olivia: confirm the p95 target you want us to optimize for (120ms or 150ms?) and share the test corpus + a short sample of traffic traces (timestamps and concurrency distribution).
- Aditya / Rafael (cc): can you prepare an initial perf matrix for A100 vs H100 and a quick checklist/runbook for the 48h run? Aim to have a draft by EOD Thu.
- Olivia: are there any compliance requirements (VPC/private endpoints) we should include in the run?

I’ll schedule the benchmark window once we have the corpus and alignment on target latency.

Thanks — Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
From: Olivia Chen <olivia@acme.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this looks great and captures the ask. A few clarifications from our side:

- Confirm p95 target: 120 ms would be ideal for the UX teams; if not possible we can accept up to 150 ms during initial rollout. Please optimize for 120 ms.
- Concurrency: sustained 16 streams, burst up to 32 for short (<= 2 min) windows.
- Throughput: we'd like reserved capacity to comfortably handle 500 tokens/sec sustained with headroom for spikes.
- We prefer H100 if it gives a clear latency/throughput benefit, but we need the comparative numbers.
- Compliance: we'll need VPC peering for the validation run (no public endpoints) and an NDA in place (legal will send a quick addendum).

I’ll upload the corpus and a 24-hour traffic sample to the Drive link you shared by EOD today. Pricing question: can you include a ballpark monthly cost for the recommended reserved sizing in the runbook?

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme AI
olivia@acme.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 13:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Dedicated capacity performance validation — post-call recap & next steps

Aditya / Rafael — forwarding Olivia's clarifications. Key asks: optimize for p95=120ms, sustained concurrency 16, reserved throughput target ~500 tokens/sec, VPC-only test.

Can you:
- Draft an initial perf matrix comparing A100 80GB vs H100 80GB for our target workload (13B–70B family models; include quantized variants). Include columns: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec per GPU, memory headroom, KV-cache size, and expected cost per token.
- Produce a short runbook for a VPC-based 48h benchmark (how we provision, required ingress from their IPs, how to stream results to a shared storage, and fallback policy).
- Estimate reserved capacity sizing and monthly cost for the recommended config (include 1: baseline, 2: target SLO configuration with headroom).

Goal: draft perf matrix + runbook by EOD Thu so we can share with Olivia and schedule the run next week. If you need extra data from Acme (sample traces, specific prompts), let me know.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia@acme.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation — scheduling + next steps

Hi Olivia — quick update. Aditya and Rafael are preparing the perf matrix and runbook; they should have a draft for you by Thu EOD.

Proposed benchmark window: Mon Apr 5 08:00–Apr 7 08:00 PT (48h). Can you confirm that works and that you’ve uploaded the corpus + 24h traffic sample to the Drive? We’ll run the validation in your VPC (we’ll request peering details) and stream results to the shared Drive folder.

We’ll include a ballpark monthly reserved capacity estimate (A100 vs H100) as part of the runbook. Also, legal noted the NDA addendum — please loop in your legal contact and we’ll get that signed before the run.

If that schedule looks good I’ll send a calendar invite and a short pre-run checklist for the engineering handoff.

Best,
Marissa
